I haven't been here long and haven't explored all the differences between here and reddit, but I can see that on the surface at least, it works mostly the same. This means that you'll end up seeing a lot of the same systemic issues reddit has. My suggestions here address a few of those issues.

Reposts: Reposts aren't bad at heart. Content will still be new to people. However, people repost simply to harvest upvotes. It also leads to piles of discussions that get repeated. My solution to this would be that duplicate links would all go to the same discussion, regardless of which sub it was posted in. Or, reposts in the same sub go to the same discussion, and discussions in other subs get linked on the side. Votes would go to the original poster or don't get counted on the reporter's count. Or some kind of split of the two.

Original content: reddit was never designed to handle oc, and it shows. I would take a page from deviant art's book to fix this. Give users a part of their page to curate their own oc, and create a 'watch' feature that gives you a simple alert (like the mail notice) when watched users post and/or comment. Perhaps to make it easier, a user account would need to set an option to be a content creator so people don't get flooded by random comments, or posting would have an option to be called OC.

Small subs: there are a number of excellent smaller subs that never really gain traction because people don't know they exist. I recommend creating subreddit tags. Example, let's say I mod a sub that is for news on pc gaming. I would give my sub the tags news, gaming, pc. Then, if a user ever did a sub search with those tags, they would find my sub. This would also allow you to make a 'subs like this' feature that would pull other subs that share keywords.

Edit: You could offer a service where websites use voat's architecture to replace the comments section of their pages. They would create a sub, and then each new article would automatically get posted there. The comments section would mirror onto the article page. It would require account creation the same way it does here. This would bring more people to voat, and would take the burden of managing comments off of their server, plus would lead to more people finding their site. It's a win all around.
